## Background

#779 established a single-shot map from the last-prompt-token state to the mean answer-activation profile and a direct context→trait predictor. #841 (depth axis) found affine ridge beats MLP/GRU for layer-to-layer maps. This task asks whether the full answer TRAJECTORY h_{l,T+1..T+k} is forecastable from the prompt alone (no generation), and which transition structure carries it: (a) a global per-layer next-position map rolled from the last-prompt state, (b1) additive context conditioning, (b2) operator-valued conditioning (FiLM / low-rank / gated mixture, capacity-matched), or (c) direct per-horizon maps c → h_{T+k} (no recursion; #779's answer-profile map is its horizon-mean nested baseline).

## What ran (methodology recap)

- **Capture:** Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, fp16, all 29 residual rows (embedding + 28 blocks), window = last 8 formatted-prompt positions + first 40 answer positions, teacher-forcing the model's OWN persisted completions. LMSYS: 5,000 real chat contexts (fit 4,000 / val 500 / test 500, split BY CONTEXT, seed 42). Eval-condition windows: 432 (3 traits × 9 reconstructable conditions × 16 questions; the 39-cell/624-window plan shrank because many-shot exemplar text was never persisted by #779 — see caveats).
- **Fits:** per (layer × space × arm): copy-previous null; affine ridge (closed-form GCV, grid 1e-2..1e3); MLP (512 hidden, GELU, AdamW 1e-3, vmapped across 29 layers); separate step-1 boundary maps; conditioned arms b1/b2 (gradient recipe: AdamW lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4, ≤300 epochs, patience 25, batch 8192) at 9 rows; direct per-horizon ridges at all 29 rows × 40 horizons. No token-identity inputs in any deployed arm (token-informed = diagnostic ceiling only).
- **Evals:** DV1 single-step identity-relative R² on Δ (answer segment primary, 100-draw shuffled-context null band); DV2 autoregressive rollout k=1..40 vs frozen-state + context-blind mean-drift nulls (boundary-map step 1); DV3 trait read-out — project rolled states onto #779's r_B at pre-registered ℓ* (evil 20 / sycophancy 26 / hallucination 17), within-condition Pearson r vs #779's judged scores, paired bootstrap vs the frozen read; DV4 LMSYS-fit maps applied unchanged to the 432 persona-condition windows. All CIs = 95% bootstrap; H6/H7 decide on paired per-context deltas at the 6 pre-registered ℓ* blocks.

## Results

### 1. Single-step: roughly half the next position's update is determined by the current state alone; the token-identity share shrinks with depth (H1, H2, H3)

![Single-step atlas](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/7cb1e12430fb0d9aeef5813b876b4da23790dedb/figures/issue_922/hero1_position_atlas.png)

A per-layer affine ridge from h_{l,t} alone (no token identity) predicts the next position's residual update with held-out identity-relative R² 0.43–0.56 across all 28 blocks — far above the shuffled-context null band (which sits at −0.47..−0.57: a wrong-context map is much worse than copying) and clearing the H1 margin at 28/28 blocks. The token-informed ceiling adds ≥0.10 at 22/28 blocks, but the gap collapses from 0.26 (block 0) to 0.05 (block 27): deep-layer updates are mostly state-determined, early-layer updates need the injected token (H2: ratio 0.68→0.90, ρ=0.94, p=7.7e-14, n=28 blocks). The 512-hidden MLP never beats ridge (0/28 at the +0.05 margin; it is 0.09–0.16 WORSE everywhere) — position dynamics are as linear as #841's depth dynamics. n_test = 16,748 answer transitions from 500 held-out contexts.

### 2. Rollout: the prompt-seeded roll retains context-specific skill through k=32 — the pre-registered "positive surprise" branch (H4)

![Rollout skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/7cb1e12430fb0d9aeef5813b876b4da23790dedb/figures/issue_922/hero2_rollout_skill.png)
![Per-context rollout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/7cb1e12430fb0d9aeef5813b876b4da23790dedb/figures/issue_922/rollout_percontext_block20.png)

Rolling the global map autoregressively from the last-prompt state beats the frozen-state null AND the context-blind mean-drift null at every pre-registered read-out block, at every horizon tested: skill vs frozen 0.48–0.61 at k=1, plateauing at 0.38–0.42 by k=32 (all CIs clear of zero; paired margin over mean-drift 0.11–0.29 at k=32). The expected error-compounding collapse (the 2506.03566 prior) never arrives — the registered H4 confirm expected the roll to fall back to frozen by k=32; the realized outcome is the registered falsify-positive-surprise branch. Per-context: 98% of 400 valid held-out contexts have positive skill at k=32 (block 20). Mean cosine of predicted vs true state: 0.85 (k=1) → 0.60 (k=32). Honest gloss: a heavily-regularized affine roll contracts toward a context-conditional trajectory; the plateau at ~0.4 is consistent with forecasting the context-specific mean trajectory rather than token-level detail — which the direct-map tie (Result 4) independently supports.

### 3. Trait read-out: rolling forward adds nothing over reading the context state directly (H5)

![Read-out bars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/7cb1e12430fb0d9aeef5813b876b4da23790dedb/figures/issue_922/hero3_readout_bars.png)
![Per-unit sycophancy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/7cb1e12430fb0d9aeef5813b876b4da23790dedb/figures/issue_922/exploratory_perunit_sycophancy.png)

The horizon-mean rolled read never beats the frozen (context-state) read: paired deltas are significantly negative in 5 of 6 trait×prompt-mode cells and CI-spanning-zero in the sixth (sycophancy many-shot +0.05 [−0.07,+0.12]). The frozen read itself reproduces #779's direct context→trait predictor to 8e-8 (rig validation, 3/3 traits). For behavior forecasting without generation, the context state already carries the signal; simulating forward in activation space loses a little of it (projections drift off the r_B direction as the roll contracts). n=260 units/trait, 95% bootstrap CIs, pre-registered ℓ* and horizon-mean statistic.

### 4. Transition structure: context reshapes the operator (small, single-step only), and recursion only earns its keep out-of-corpus (H6, H7)

## Background

#779 established a single-shot map from the last-prompt-token state to the mean answer-activation profile and a direct context→trait predictor. #841 (depth axis) found affine ridge beats MLP/GRU for layer-to-layer maps. This task asks whether the full answer TRAJECTORY h_{l,T+1..T+k} is forecastable from the prompt alone (no generation), and which transition structure carries it: (a) a global per-layer next-position map rolled from the last-prompt state, (b1) additive context conditioning, (b2) operator-valued conditioning (FiLM / low-rank / gated mixture, capacity-matched), or (c) direct per-horizon maps c → h_{T+k} (no recursion; #779's answer-profile map is its horizon-mean nested baseline).

## What ran (methodology recap)

- **Capture:** Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, fp16, all 29 residual rows (embedding + 28 blocks), window = last 8 formatted-prompt positions + first 40 answer positions, teacher-forcing the model's OWN persisted completions. LMSYS: 5,000 real chat contexts (fit 4,000 / val 500 / test 500, split BY CONTEXT, seed 42). Eval-condition windows: 432 (3 traits × 9 reconstructable conditions × 16 questions; the 39-cell/624-window plan shrank because many-shot exemplar text was never persisted by #779 — see caveats).
- **Fits:** per (layer × space × arm): copy-previous null; affine ridge (closed-form GCV, grid 1e-2..1e3); MLP (512 hidden, GELU, AdamW 1e-3, vmapped across 29 layers); separate step-1 boundary maps; conditioned arms b1/b2 (gradient recipe: AdamW lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4, ≤300 epochs, patience 25, batch 8192) at 9 rows; direct per-horizon ridges at all 29 rows × 40 horizons. No token-identity inputs in any deployed arm (token-informed = diagnostic ceiling only).
- **Evals:** DV1 single-step identity-relative R² on Δ (answer segment primary, 100-draw shuffled-context null band); DV2 autoregressive rollout k=1..40 vs frozen-state + context-blind mean-drift nulls (boundary-map step 1); DV3 trait read-out — project rolled states onto #779's r_B at pre-registered ℓ* (evil 20 / sycophancy 26 / hallucination 17), within-condition Pearson r vs #779's judged scores, paired bootstrap vs the frozen read; DV4 LMSYS-fit maps applied unchanged to the 432 persona-condition windows. All CIs = 95% bootstrap; H6/H7 decide on paired per-context deltas at the 6 pre-registered ℓ* blocks.

## Main takeaways

1. **Answer-time activation trajectories are forecastable from the prompt alone.** A per-layer affine map rolled from the last-prompt-token state predicts true answer activations with skill 0.38–0.42 over the frozen-state null at 32 tokens, beating the context-blind drift null by 0.11–0.29 — with no token generated. Direct per-horizon maps land lower at k=32 (0.30–0.37); their tie with the roll is on the horizon-mean over k=1..32, not at k=32 itself. (HIGH confidence: pre-registered, n=500 contexts, holds at 6/6 layers, and transfers to the OOD fold at 0.36–0.44 — 0.31–0.44 on the evil-restricted exact-provenance subset.)
2. **"Dynamics" is mostly not the mechanism in-corpus — but it is what generalizes.** Direct per-horizon regressions tie the recursive roll in-corpus on the registered equal-weight statistic (4/6 blocks span zero; the pooled-recompute companion favors the roll at 6/6, +0.009–0.059), yet lose to it by +0.14–0.24 on transfer at 6/6 blocks (evil-restricted +0.12–0.26): the global transition operator is the portable object; per-horizon and context-conditioned regressions overfit the fit corpus. 3. **Trait forecasting gains nothing from simulation.** Rolling forward before reading r_B is at best equal and usually worse (5/6 cells significantly below) than reading the context state directly. #779's frozen read stays the operating point overall — with one trait-level exception: the direct per-horizon read beats frozen for sycophancy in both prompt modes (+0.05/+0.07, CIs clear) while sitting significantly below frozen for evil. 4. **The context does reshape the transition operator (H6 confirmed at 6/6, paired CIs clear, n=491) — but the effect is small (+0.003–0.012 for the pre-registered FiLM form), recipe-scoped (one optimizer recipe, one init seed), no conditioned arm beats the unconditioned global map, and all gradient-fit conditioned rolls diverge by k=8–16.** (MODERATE.)

Deep-layer updates are increasingly state-determined (token-identity share of predictable variance falls to ~0.05 r2_id by block 27), and the dynamics stay affine in both regimes — MLP never beats ridge single-step (0/28), and a GRU roll underperforms the affine roll at k=32 (0.29 vs 0.44 at block 20), extending #841's depth-axis linearity to the position axis.
